clue.text: I seem dreadful, being badly cast in operetta

indicators.note: something badly cast is poorly arranged, so these letters must be put in a new order

explanation.surface: A performer frets that their own poor casting will ruin a light opera production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly cast' signals rearranging the letters of I SEEM DREADFUL; 'being' just links the definition. The theatrical surface makes 'cast' look like the actors, not the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Strauss II's comic stage work about a masked ball is a famous Viennese operetta.

clue.text: Be stubborn, yet make an impression at ground level?

definitions.text: make an impression at ground level?

explanation.surface: Someone digs in their heels in a dispute while also leaving a mark on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: pressing the backs of the shoes into the soil leaves a dent at ground level, which the question mark flags as playful.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to refuse to yield, and taken literally it describes pushing the backs of one's feet into the earth.

clue.text: Ecstasy over no marks in the 3 rs? That can't be right!

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means it sits above, so it comes first

parts.note: E is the common slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: the zero is placed inside the run of three R letters

parts.note: the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, giving three R letters
no marks is a score of zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A pupil on drugs scores nothing in basic schooling, and the teacher protests at the result.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are the traditional basics of schooling: reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic. The definition is an exclamation, read as 'that's a mistake'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry that something cannot be right means there has been a mistake.

clue.text: Something in hardware store is soiled line thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters are tossed about and land in a different order

explanation.surface: A dirty fishing line gets discarded among the stock of a hardware shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' reads as discarding the line, but it signals rearranging SOILED LINE; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax-seed oil, used for treating wood and cricket bats, is sold in hardware shops.

clue.text: Very determined to make entrance — girl with energy

parts.note: a door is an entrance to a room or building
Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A young woman with plenty of energy is set on making a grand entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a desperate, all-out resolve where failure is not an option.

clue.text: Illegal cigarettes in refrigerated ships

explanation.surface: Smugglers hide marijuana joints in the cargo of cold-storage vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for marijuana joints and is also a name for refrigerated cargo vessels.

clue.text: A small room with society members

parts.note: RM is the standard short form of room, the shortening signalled by small

explanation.surface: A club crams its members into one tiny room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' looks like club members, but here it means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs are sometimes called members, and the arms are two of them.

clue.text: Idiot's uncomplicated fashion

parts.note: uncomplicated means simple
ton is an old word for fashion or style, as in 'bon ton'

explanation.surface: A fool dresses in a plain, unfussy style.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay. TON for fashion is a crossword favourite from the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or dimwit is called by this name.

clue.text: Game span cut down at first

indicators.note: this tells us the word for cut down is placed before the word for span

parts.note: to cut down something is to reduce or shrink it, to contract it
a bridge spans a river, so span gives bridge

explanation.surface: A bridge span is being dismantled from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' moves the reduction word ahead of the span word, though the clue gives them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the most common form of the four-player card game played with bidding and tricks.

clue.text: Do realign mispositioned chandelier

indicators.note: mispositioned means put in the wrong place, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to straighten a light fitting hung crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mispositioned' signals rearranging DO REALIGN. The definition is an ornate branched candle holder or chandelier.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an elaborate branched candlestick or light fitting, a kind of chandelier.

clue.text: Dance with maiden in front of the pulpit

indicators.note: this puts the letter for maiden before the word for pulpit

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
an ambo is a raised pulpit or reading desk in early churches

explanation.surface: A young woman dances right in front of the preacher's stand in church.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring a maiden (an over with no runs) is written M. AMBO is an old word for a church pulpit; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lively Latin American ballroom dance originating in Cuba.

clue.text: Health worker making rush back to home counties

indicators.note: back means the word for rush is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to rush is to run
the Home Counties around London lie in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A medic dashes back to the leafy counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the South East (SE). 'making' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital carer who tends patients is a key health worker.

clue.text: River gentle but not shallow

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
P stands for piano, the musical instruction to play softly or gently

explanation.surface: A gently flowing river that is nonetheless far from shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland. P (piano) means soft in music; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with great distance from top to bottom is the opposite of shallow.

clue.text: Scheme to get power, meeting destiny

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's destiny

explanation.surface: A schemer seeks power as if it were their fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret plan or conspiracy is a scheme.

clue.text: Writer's little bag obtainable from nice places

indicators.note: the answer is obtainable from these letters by rearranging them

explanation.surface: An author's small pouch can be bought in pleasant shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtainable from' suggests buying, but it signals that the letters of NICE PLACES make the answer. The 'writer' is a pen or pencil, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A school pouch holding pens and pencils is a small bag for writing implements.

clue.text: Do start deteriorating left among pigs

indicators.note: among means the letters go inside the word for pigs

parts.note: swine is another word for pigs

indicators.note: start means take only the first letter of deteriorating

explanation.surface: A pig farm begins to go downhill, with one animal left among the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb of doing, but it is slang for cheat. The start of 'deteriorating' and L go inside SWINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for cheating or conning them.

clue.text: I am worker full of drink being pompous

indicators.note: full of means the word for drink is packed inside the other pieces

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords, from the worker ant
port is a fortified wine, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being a drunken labourer who is full of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts the drink between I'M and the worker; 'being' is a link. The definition is the sense 'self-important', as in 'an important little man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-important or pompous people act as though they are of great consequence.

clue.text: Ranges of colours etc. Shown by various carpets

indicators.note: various suggests differing forms, so the letters of carpets are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Lots of rugs display a whole range of colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' signals rearranging CARPETS; 'Shown by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bands of colour, such as those made by a prism, are the plural of a range of wavelengths.

clue.text: What troubles me is pet — result of milk consumption?

indicators.note: troubles here means disturbs or stirs up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A grumble that a spoilt pet is the thing that bothers me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' signals rearranging ME IS PET; 'What' is a link. Drinking the milk leaves bottles that go back to the milkman.
explanation.definitionFit: Once the milk is drunk, the used bottles left behind are the outcome of drinking it.

clue.text: A little something to sip before study

indicators.note: before means the sipping word comes first

parts.note: soup is a liquid food one can sip
to con is an old word meaning to study or learn

explanation.surface: A student has a light snack to drink before settling down to revise.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is spelt with a cedilla in French. CON for study is an old verb still common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny trace or hint of something is a small amount, from the French.

clue.text: Clown, crazy person getting the prize at fairground?

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown
a nut is slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A clown and a madman between them win the top fairground reward.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a famous circus performer. At a British fair the coconut shy rewards those who knock a nut off its stand; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: At a coconut shy, the stall prize is the hard-shelled tropical nut itself.

clue.text: Nude in naughty act in nightclub

indicators.note: in means the word for nude is placed inside the rearranged act
naughty suggests misbehaving letters that are put in a new order

parts.note: nude means bare

explanation.surface: A risqué nude routine is performed at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' scrambles the clue's 'act' into CAT; the first 'in' is the container signal and the second is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub or restaurant offering live entertainment and floor shows is known by this French word.

clue.text: Parrot's resplendent brightness not initially seen

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped from the word for resplendent brightness

parts.note: glory is radiant splendour or brightness

explanation.surface: A parrot's brilliant plumage goes unnoticed at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is'; 'seen' is a link. This bird is a small brightly coloured parrot of Australasia.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small, brightly coloured Australasian parrot related to the lorikeet.

clue.text: Greek character goes to doctor having lost feeling

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A Greek patient visits the doctor after losing sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to' joins the two pieces. 'character' means a letter here, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Without sensation, as after an anaesthetic, a body part is deadened.

clue.text: Concealed in school, a seriously powerful electronic device

indicators.note: concealed in tells us the answer lies within the words school, a seriously

explanation.surface: A dangerous gadget has been smuggled into a school.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'school', the word 'a' and the start of 'seriously'.
explanation.definitionFit: A device emitting a narrow intense beam of light is a powerful piece of electronics.

clue.text: Wickedness is considered very good on this penisula

parts.note: sin is wickedness
A1 means first-class or very good, with the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: Evil is thought to be excellent in this desert land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penisula' is the clue's misspelling of peninsula. A1 (first-rate) becomes AI with the figure 1 read as I; 'is considered' and 'on this' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular desert land between Africa and Asia in Egypt is a peninsula.

clue.text: Why person is given this publicity

indicators.note: the words Why person are given the answer within them, held across the join

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a particular person is getting all this media attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words: the end of 'Why' and the start of 'person'.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive promotion or media buzz around something is publicity.

clue.text: I agree one of the two learners must leave country

indicators.note: must leave means one letter is taken out of the phrase for I agree

parts.note: I tally means my account matches, so I agree
L is the learner sign, and the phrase for I agree holds two of them

explanation.surface: A pair of trainee drivers are told one of them must quit the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I tally' means 'I agree'; drop one of its two L's (L-plates mark a learner driver) to leave the country.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the boot-shaped Mediterranean country, a nation in southern Europe.

clue.text: Like living room, for instance, with new cedar unit

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of cedar unit

explanation.surface: A lounge gets a brand-new cedar storage cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals rearranging CEDAR UNIT; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A living room with drapes at its windows fits this description, as an example.

clue.text: Eileen tonight — wild or conforming?

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters of Eileen tonight are mixed up

explanation.surface: Will Eileen let loose this evening or behave herself?
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' signals rearranging EILEEN TONIGHT; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means obeying the rules, like runners keeping their feet at the starting mark.
